title: Archon configuration
description: Configuration for Archon, found by walking up from the analysed path. Generated by 'archon schema' from the rules currently registered.

$schema.description: Path to this schema. Ignored by Archon; read by editors.

rules.description: Severity per rule id, or per category to set a whole family at once. An explicit rule id always wins over its category.

AR0001.description: Layer dependency violation (architecture, file scope, default warning). A layer references another layer that the configured rules forbid.

AR0002.description: Singleton captures scoped service (lifetime, workspace scope, default error). A singleton holds a scoped service, which scope validation rejects at runtime.

AR0003.description: Singleton captures transient service (lifetime, workspace scope, default warning). A singleton holds a transient service, so that service never leaves memory.

AR0004.description: Scoped service captures transient service (lifetime, workspace scope, default information). A scoped service holds a transient service for the lifetime of the scope.

AR0005.description: Dependency has no visible registration (lifetime, workspace scope, default off). A constructor parameter matches no registration found in the workspace.

AR0010.description: Blocking on a task (async, file scope, default warning). A task is blocked on with .Result, .Wait() or .GetAwaiter().GetResult() instead of awaited.

AR0011.description: Task result discarded (async, file scope, default warning). A task-returning call is neither awaited nor assigned, so its failures are lost.

AR0012.description: async void method (async, file scope, default warning). An async void method cannot be awaited and its exceptions cannot be caught by the caller.

AR0013.description: Exception discarded (async, file scope, default warning). An empty catch block hides a failure completely.

AR0014.description: Rethrow resets the stack trace (async, file scope, default warning). 'throw ex;' inside a catch block resets the stack trace to this line instead of preserving where the exception actually originated. Use a bare 'throw;' instead.

AR0015.description: Thread.Sleep in an async method (async, file scope, default warning). An async method blocks its thread with Thread.Sleep instead of awaiting Task.Delay, holding the thread for no reason.

AR0020.description: Count used as an emptiness check (performance, file scope, default information). A sequence is counted in full to decide whether it holds anything; Any stops at the first element.

AR0021.description: String concatenation in a loop (performance, file scope, default information). Repeated concatenation in a loop copies the whole string each time.

AR0022.description: Sequence materialised then transformed (performance, file scope, default hint). A sequence is copied into a list or array and then immediately filtered or transformed again.

AR0023.description: Wildcard column list in inline SQL (performance, file scope, default information). SQL embedded in C# selects all columns, so its result changes whenever a table does.

AR0030.description: Configuration key not found in settings (configuration, project scope, default warning). A configuration key read in code appears in none of the settings files beside the project.

AR0031.description: Settings file could not be read (configuration, project scope, default information). A settings file could not be parsed, so keys could not be checked against it.

AR0040.description: Project reference cycle (architecture, workspace scope, default error). Two or more projects reference each other, directly or through intermediaries.

AR0041.description: Project file could not be read (architecture, workspace scope, default information). A project file could not be parsed, so its references were not included in the graph.

AR0050.description: Hardcoded credential (security, file scope, default warning). A non-empty string literal is assigned to a name that reads as a credential, so the value may be a real secret committed to source.

AR0051.description: Weak cryptographic primitive (security, file scope, default warning). A cryptographic type known to be weak by its written name is constructed or invoked.

AR0052.description: System.Random used for a security-shaped value (security, file scope, default information). System.Random is not cryptographically secure; a value named for a security purpose may need RandomNumberGenerator instead.

AR0053.description: Regular expression can backtrack catastrophically (security, file scope, default warning). A quantified group is itself quantified, so a crafted input can make matching take exponential time.

AR0054.description: SQL built by concatenation or interpolation (security, file scope, default warning). A SQL command is built by string concatenation or interpolation instead of a parameterised query, risking SQL injection.

AR0060.description: Method is hard to follow (complexity, file scope, default warning). A method's nested and branching control flow has crossed the configured threshold.

AR0061.description: String literal repeated in this file (complexity, file scope, default information). The same non-trivial string literal appears several times; an edit to one copy can silently miss the rest.

AR0070.description: Parameter is never used (maintainability, file scope, default hint). A method parameter is never read in the method body. Silent whenever the signature might not be free to change, since that cannot always be told from syntax alone.

AR0071.description: Local variable is never used (maintainability, file scope, default information). A local variable is declared and never read again.

AR0072.description: Condition is always true or always false (maintainability, file scope, default information). A literal boolean condition or a self-comparison decides nothing; the branch it guards is either dead or unconditional.

AR0073.description: Console used directly for output (maintainability, file scope, default hint). Console.Write/WriteLine bypasses structured logging. Expected in a project that is itself a console entry point, which this rule cannot tell apart from any other file.

AR0074.description: Disposable local is never disposed (maintainability, file scope, default warning). A local variable creates a well-known disposable type and is never disposed, passed on, returned or assigned onward on any path this rule can see.

AR0075.description: Mutable field exposed as public (maintainability, file scope, default information). A public, non-readonly field on a class lets any caller change its value directly, with no chance to validate or react. Expose a property instead.

AR0080.description: Unknown column referenced in inline SQL (sql, workspace scope, default warning). SQL embedded in C# names a column that does not exist on the table it targets, judged against CREATE TABLE statements found elsewhere in the workspace.

AR0090.description: Culture-sensitive string casing (globalization, file scope, default information). ToUpper()/ToLower() cast case using the current culture, which can silently change letters under some cultures (e.g. Turkish 'i'). Use ToUpperInvariant()/ToLowerInvariant() unless the result is shown to the user in their own culture.

SQ0001.description: Wildcard column list (sql, file scope, default warning). A statement selects all columns instead of naming the ones it uses.

SQ0002.description: Statement could not be parsed (sql, file scope, default information). A file could not be parsed as T-SQL, so no SQL rule was able to inspect it.

SQ0010.description: Table hint policy (sql, file scope, default warning). A table reference does not follow the configured policy on locking hints.

SQ0011.description: Temporary table naming (sql, file scope, default warning). A temporary table's name does not match the configured pattern.

SQ0012.description: Stored procedure naming (sql, file scope, default warning). A stored procedure's name does not match the configured pattern.

SQ0020.description: DELETE/UPDATE with no WHERE clause (sql, file scope, default warning). A DELETE or UPDATE statement has no WHERE clause, so it applies to every row in the table.

SQ0021.description: Comparison to NULL with = or <> (sql, file scope, default warning). A comparison to NULL with '=' or '<>' is always unknown under three-valued logic; use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL instead.

additionalProperties.description: Severity for a rule id this installation does not have registered, such as one from a rule pack that is not currently loadable.

exclude.description: Path globs never analysed, relative to the workspace root. Added to the defaults (bin, obj, node_modules, .git) rather than replacing them.

layers.description: Layer definitions and permitted dependency direction. AR0001 stays silent until "layers" declares at least one layer.

mode.description: denylist forbids only the edges in "deny"; allowlist permits only those in "allow". Anything else is treated as denylist, which is the permissive reading.

layers.description: Layer name to the namespace prefixes belonging to it. A file whose namespace matches no prefix is never flagged.

id.description: A name for this edge, quoted back in the finding message.

from.description: The referencing layer. Must match a key of "layers" exactly; case is significant.

to.description: The referenced layer. Must match a key of "layers" exactly; case is significant.

deny.description: Forbidden edges. Read only when mode is denylist.

id.description: A name for this edge, quoted back in the finding message.

from.description: The referencing layer. Must match a key of "layers" exactly; case is significant.

to.description: The referenced layer. Must match a key of "layers" exactly; case is significant.

allow.description: Permitted edges. Read only when mode is allowlist.

rulePacks.description: Assembly paths providing additional IRulePack implementations, absolute or relative to the workspace root. A pack that fails to load is reported and skipped.

options.description: Per-rule option objects, keyed by rule id. A rule that reads none ignores its entry.

overrides.description: Settings applied only to files matching a block's globs, layered over the top-level ones. Later blocks win over earlier ones where both match a file; within a block a rule id wins over its category, and a block's category entry wins over a top-level rule id.

files.description: Path globs, relative to the workspace root, selecting the files this block applies to.
